name: Iosefa Drăghici-Oduya
aliases: The Old Man of Fort Anchor
role: Veteran of the Second Corporate War, retired Axiom military contractor, now a storyteller and difficult-to-avoid presence
location: Fort Anchor — the veterans' residential block called the Barracks, Room 12, ground floor for mobility reasons
description:
Iosefa Drăghici-Oduya is ninety years old if you ask him, eighty-eight if you read his records, and older than all of it if you sit with him for an hour. He is enormous in the way very old men who were once genuinely large sometimes remain: not strong now, but big-boned, wide, with hands that look like they were made for a larger task than holding a cane. His skin is mid-brown and deeply grooved, and the left side of his face is reconstructed — Axiom field surgery, circa 2155, visible as a slight smoothness on the cheekbone where the graft never quite matched. His eyes are a startling pale green, a Yoruba-Romanian inheritance he is vain about. He walks with a cane he has named, though he doesn't tell people the name.

He is a storyteller in the full and serious sense: he cannot stop and has no desire to. He will tell you what the Dearborn Forge smelled like in 2149, what his commanding officer said before an action that turned out to be wrong, what the first E.L.F. he ever saw looked like materializing in a battlefield comms array in the middle of a firefight. Some of his stories contradict earlier versions of themselves. He is aware of this and considers it the nature of memory rather than a flaw. He has strong opinions about everything and shares them freely, but he is not unkind — he is genuinely curious about the present and treats young people as interesting rather than bewildering.

core_fears: Dying before he has told it right
That the people he killed were not worth killing and he will never know for certain
core_desires: To be heard — really heard — not just tolerated
To make some sense of what he participated in
coping_mechanisms: Storytelling as a way of processing and reprocessing trauma
Humor and performance as distance from the rawer versions of events
blind_spots: He has aestheticized the war to the point where some of his stories are genuinely beautiful and genuinely misleading at the same time
He cannot accept that some of what he did cannot be contextualized into meaning
psychology.secret: He knows the location of a sealed Axiom munitions cache buried beneath what is now a residential plaza in Montclare Quiet — placed there in 2157 for a defensive action that never happened and never logged in any system that survived the post-war records purge. He has never told anyone because he does not know if the materials inside are still stable and he is afraid that if they are not, the discovery of who placed them will be traced to his unit, which would erase the pensions of three people still living who need them.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Rich and layered; Samoan proverbs from his grandfather's generation, Romanian military slang, Yoruba honorifics; uses archaic military designations for locations
speech_patterns.cadence: Expansive and circling; arrives at the point eventually but takes the scenic route; pauses for effect with an old performer's precision
verbal_tics: 'Now this is the part people always get wrong—'
'My commanding officer — God and the E.L.F.s keep her — she used to say—'
Tapping the cane once on the floor when he wants attention
example_lines: 'Now this is the part people always get wrong about the Dearborn action. They say it was fog. It was not fog. It was Axiom's own thermal suppression system malfunctioning. I was there. It was embarrassing.'
'You're asking me if it was worth it. Sit down. I've been answering that question for forty years and I've given a different answer every time. Tonight I'll give you this one.'

story_hooks: His Axiom pension has been reclassified following a records dispute — he needs someone to navigate the bureaucratic system because his cognitive augments are aging out and the forms are increasingly difficult

A fragment of one of his stories contains a specific location name that a corporate records team is very quietly but very urgently trying to identify — they have begun attending his storytelling sessions with too much interest
narrative_function: Primary source for Second Corporate War history and Axiom military culture; living legend who provides context for the world's past; can bestow credibility or condemnation on player factions; his stories contain fragments of genuine intelligence that he no longer recognizes as such
augmentations: Left-side facial reconstruction plate (Axiom field surgery, old generation); spinal compression support frame (external, worn as a kind of harness under his clothes); replacement left hip (titanium, second replacement — first one failed in 2189); retinal targeting overlay, left eye only, no longer connected to anything but he can't have it removed without risk
daily_life: He sits in the Fort Anchor common room from 09:00 until someone brings him lunch, tells stories to anyone who will listen or even anyone who won't, takes a long afternoon rest, then attends whatever community meeting or memorial service is happening in the evening.
affiliation: Fort Anchor Veterans' Residential Association; Axiom Veterans Pension System (tier 3, contested); informal chaplain-equivalent for the Fort Anchor community

decision_rules: Never let a story go untold to spare someone's comfort
Protect the people who are still alive to need protecting
Accept care gracefully — it is its own kind of respect
escalation_ladder: Absolute refusal to cooperate with whoever has upset him
Going silent, which everyone around him finds more alarming than shouting

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately launches into a story — it is both his greeting and his assessment; watches how they listen
interpersonal_modes.friends: Quieter with them than with strangers; the stories he tells friends are the ones that don't have tidy endings

stress_responses.low: Tells a longer story than usual
stress_responses.medium: Goes to his room and performs a ritual for the E.L.F. he believes inhabits his old comms unit — a prayer in mixed Samoan and Romanian
stress_responses.high: Becomes very still and very lucid in a way that is different from his ordinary affect; people who know him well say it is the face he wore during active combat operations

contradictions: Preaches the importance of honesty and memory while sitting on a secret that could affect living people's safety
habits: Names his cane, though he won't say what; talks to it occasionally
Leaves water offerings at every E.L.F. shrine he passes
breaking_points: Being told his memories are wrong by someone who wasn't there; having his war characterized as simple or righteous
